paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how coverage changes as the number of sampled completions increases for four model variants (Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT). The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (k)” and is shown on a logarithmic base-2 scale with tick labels from \(2^0\) through \(2^8\) (i.e., k = 1 to 256) at every integer exponent. The y-axis is labeled “Coverage” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from about 0.2 up to just under 1.0, with major tick marks visible at approximately 0.2 intervals (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8). The Llama-3B series is drawn as a solid blue line with circular markers and increases steadily from about 0.43 at \(2^0\) to about 0.92 at \(2^8\), passing near 0.62 at \(2^2\), ~0.78 at \(2^4\), and ~0.87 at \(2^6\). The Llama-3B + FT series is drawn as a green dotted line with upward triangle markers and similarly rises from about 0.43–0.44 at \(2^0\) to about 0.92–0.93 at \(2^8\), with intermediate points around ~0.64 at \(2^2\), ~0.79 at \(2^4\), and ~0.88 at \(2^6\). The Llama-1B series is drawn as a solid light-blue line with circular markers and increases from about 0.25 at \(2^0\) to about 0.86–0.87 at \(2^8\), with visible points around ~0.44 at \(2^2\), ~0.60 at \(2^4\), and ~0.79–0.80 at \(2^6\). The Llama-1B + FT series is drawn as a light-green dotted line with upward triangle markers and increases from about 0.25–0.26 at \(2^0\) to about 0.88–0.89 at \(2^8\), with intermediate values around ~0.45 at \(2^2\), ~0.62 at \(2^4\), and ~0.82 at \(2^6\); all four lines show a monotonic upward progression across the full x-axis range.
